title: Axiom Math wants to keep AI slop out of mathematics
slides: Can AI do math without inventing false proofs?
Axiom Math raised funding to build formal verification
Its system checks every step against proof assistants
Researchers can submit results and get machine-verified
Demand proof, not prose, from every AI math claim
thread_text:
1. AI math needs proof

Axiom Math just raised funding to build formal verification for AI-generated proofs. The goal: ensure every step is machine-checked, not just plausible.

2. Proof assistants as judges

The system checks each step against proof assistants. These are software tools that verify mathematical correctness, leaving no room for invented steps.

3. Submit your results

Researchers can now submit their results and get them machine-verified. This could speed up peer review and increase trust in AI-assisted math.

4. Demand proof, not prose

When an AI claims a math result, ask for the proof. With formal verification, you can check it step by step instead of trusting the model's narrative.

5. Test it yourself

Next time an AI gives you a math answer, ask it to show its work. If it can't provide a verifiable proof, treat it as a guess.

instagram.caption:
An AI can now generate a math proof that looks perfect and is completely wrong. Axiom Math raised funding to catch exactly that. 🔍

Its system checks every single step against proof assistants, software that verifies correctness mechanically.

No plausible-sounding leaps, no invented steps.

Researchers can submit results and get them machine-verified before anyone trusts them.

If you use AI for calculations, ask it to show its work.

Would you be able to tell a real proof from a confident fake? 🧮
